meta.title: Grove State Is the RAM
meta.subtitle: The graph image is ROM shared by every entity, so anything a node remembers has to live somewhere else — a hash map inside a buffer on the entity

views.label: Read-only, and writable
views.note: One image, thousands of entities. Nothing in the image can be per-entity, so none of it is.

views.label: Why the key is so wide
views.note: Graph, then owner scope, then a local number. Two graphs on one entity never collide.

views.label: Inside the buffer
views.note: Buckets, keys, sizes and a bump-allocated value arena, all inside one dynamic buffer.

views.label: Who writes to it
views.note: Nodes keep their own memory here. So does the state machine — its cursor is just another key.

components.label: Buffer on the entity
components.sublabel: moves with the entity, saves with it

components.label: Buckets and keys
components.sublabel: an open hash map, laid out by offset

boundaries.label: one dynamic buffer · header, buckets, keys, sizes and values in a single allocation

cards.title: The split, and why it exists
items: The image is one blob shared by every entity running that graph
So a node cannot own a field — there is exactly one copy of the node
Everything remembered lives in one buffer · Grove BovineLabs.Grove/Core/GroveState.cs:13

cards.title: Untyped means the value size varies
items: Each entry's size is stored beside it as a small integer
Values are bump allocated into a data region in the same buffer · same file:319
So one map holds a bool next to a snapshot next to a node id

cards.title: What the key protects you from
items: Graph id, scope id and two more words · Grove BovineLabs.Grove/Core/GroveStateKey.cs:12
Graph id first, so two graphs on one entity cannot alias
Scope id next, so two copies of one node keep separate memory
Tear a graph down by that first word · Grove BovineLabs.Grove/Core/GraphStateUtil.cs:60
